subject: Hightower Capital — ask: per-tenant KV-cache eviction controls for latency-sensitive workloads
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hightower Cap — per-tenant KV-cache eviction control (priority ask)

Team —

Quick one: Hightower (prospect, SERIOUS buyer; procurement ready pending SOW) surfaced a blocker in yesterday’s POE call. Their engineering lead, Alex Chen, said their production traffic pattern includes a heavy mix of short, latency-sensitive inference requests for high-value accounts and a background bulk workload for low-value accounts. They want the ability to force eviction/pinning of specific tenant keys (TTL overrides and an explicit "pin") so hot tenants don’t get evicted by large background jobs.

Why it matters: without this control they claim 30–40% latency regressions during peak batch jobs — they’re pushing for it as a gating item for the SOW. They asked for an engineering commitment window (<= 8 weeks preferred) and to see a short design sketch.

Asks: can product/eng confirm feasibility and a rough timeline? If we can’t meet strict pinning semantics, what are acceptable mitigations (priority lanes, soft-reservations, per-tenant cache quotas, or application-level affinity)?

I’ve attached the current SOW and their redlines — procurement is watching. Any way we can scope a trimmed-down deliverable for an initial commit?

Thanks — I’m on their call at 11:00 PT today and should be able to push for phased acceptance if we can offer an interim plan.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the SOW/redlines. Quick read-through notes below. High level: this is feasible but non-trivial — there are three surfaces to consider:

- API surface: new per-tenant cache control endpoints (pin/unpin, set-ttl-override, list-pins).
- Runtime behavior: eviction policy modifications so pinned keys are exempt from batch-driven evictions; interactions with our continuous batching and prefix cache.
- Safety/operational: telemetry, admin controls, and a kill-switch to roll back if memory pressure spikes.

Questions for engineering (Jonas):
1) Is there a straightforward path to implement a per-tenant pin flag that integrates with our existing KV shard eviction loop? Rough idea would be a small bit on the tenant metadata that the eviction iterator checks.
2) Worst-case engineering estimate for an MVP (no UI): design + one eng + one QA + ops validation -> how many sprints?
3) Can we offer a short-term mitigation (priority lane) that requires no runtime change, e.g., routing their critical traffic to a dedicated pool or reserved capacity while we build the feature?

If we can get an engineering estimate and a proposed rollout plan (canary -> tenant opt-in -> full release), I can draft a short product note for procurement to keep signing moving.

Marissa

Marissa / Rishi —

Short answer: doable, but the engineering scope is larger than a single flag. Sketch of tradeoffs and a realistic plan below.

Technical tradeoffs:
- Option A (pin bit on tenant metadata): simplest change to eviction loop; risk: if many tenants are pinned, memory pressure could spike and cause OOMs. Must pair with safeguards (global pinned cap, eviction of low-priority pinned keys after threshold).
- Option B (per-tenant quota + soft-reserve): stricter control over memory use; more invasive (changes to accounting, shard-level quotas). Better long-term but 2x effort.
- Option C (routing to reserved pool): zero runtime change to main eviction logic; just requires reserved capacity (Dedicated or burst pool) and routing rules. Quick but costly for the customer and not ideal for long term.

MVP proposal (to unblock deal quickly):
1) Short term (<=2 weeks): Offer to route their 5 highest-value tenants to a small reserved pool we control (Option C). Ops/Provisioning can set this up; would require a short contract amendment for reserved capacity pricing. Low engineering risk.
2) Mid term (8–10 weeks): Implement Option A (pin bit) with safety limits, plus telemetry and an opt-in canary for Hightower. This is a single-engineer + part-time QA + part-time SRE project (approx 3 sprints).
3) Long term (Q4): Rework to Option B for robust per-tenant quotas and better accounting.

Operational requirements: admin UI / CLI for pin management (we can keep this internal initially), metrics on pinned count/mem usage, and a kill-switch for emergency unpin.

Estimate: MVP routing mitigation — 2–4 days to provision and test. Pin-bit MVP — design + 3x2-week sprints (approx 6 weeks) for initial implementation, plus 2 weeks for QA and ops validation -> 8 weeks total.

I can draft a lightweight design doc today if we need it for procurement. If they require guarantees (SLA) around pinned behavior we need to limit the number of pinned tenants and document failure modes.

—Jonas
